scope: Permanent native server-reward receipts and legacy version-3 SQL queue recovery; current production delivery uses the Wolverine extension, not a complete war settlement

history_review.preserved: Recipient selection, reward amounts/templates/counts, item attribute linking, coins, mail type, net-string framing, native DB item allocation and the existing SQL queue order. No custom rewards or publisher balance changes.
history_review.reason: The previous helper committed the header independently, swallowed attachment errors and could leave an empty paid reward or lose an unawaited write on process exit. This is a persistence/integrity repair.

implementation: MailOperator is a synchronous producer of an immutable version-3 TCharacterSaveQueue record. Its complete intent commits to SQL before even an ignored Task returns; a failed enqueue cannot silently fall back to the old partial write.

The intent freezes operation GUID, recipient ID/name, mail type/text/time/coins and all new-item attributes. Version-1/2 character and quest queue records remain readable. Invalid, duplicate-ID or mixed records reject before enqueue.

Migration 045 adds TOperatorPostOperation. One SQL transaction covers native TSavePost, native DB item-ID allocation, all native TSaveItemDirect attachments, row verification, containment and the receipt.

Replaying the same GUID and payload returns its receipt without issuing again, including after the letter was collected/deleted. Changed content under an issued GUID is rejected. Receipt rows must be retained with the matching game database and queue.

A transaction lock serializes .NET mail writers; the native item allocator's persisted domain is separate from the Map counter. An already-owned generated item ID is rejected before the native delete/insert can overwrite it.
The recipient's current SQL name is resolved by ID. A deleted recipient produces a durable rejection instead of orphan mail or an endlessly blocked FIFO queue.

Startup requires the receipt schema before recovery/client acceptance. Pending delivery is replayed through the existing SQL DB lane/startup/login barriers. Online notifications run through the actor callback queue only for a newly committed letter.

Shared callers audited: fort/castle/mission/Sky Garden rewards, arena fee rewards, RPS rewards, tournament invitations/bets and cash-bonus error replacement. DB-free fixtures retain their fake-store path; configured SQL always uses the durable path. Existing-item MailItemBack and ordinary player mail are separate transfer paths.

validation.platform: Linux .NET 10, isolated SDK builds and disposable SQL Server
validation.fixture: 41 exported native table shapes, 29 native procedures, synthetic data only; migrations 041 through 045 applied only in the disposable instance.
checks: Migration applies twice and missing required schema fails startup storage verification
Native header, money, all attachment fields and canonical recipient name roundtrip
Plain and money-only letters preserve type/containment without allocating item IDs
Concurrent SQL writers deduplicate one accepted operation
Changed payload rejects; claimed/deleted mail cannot be recreated by receipt replay
Second attachment failure rolls back header, prior attachment, money, ID allocation and receipt
Silent native item insertion failure is detected and rolls the reward back
Receipt-write failure rolls native writes back; retry can complete once
Corrupted allocator cannot overwrite an existing inventory item
Missing recipient creates only a durable rejection receipt
Real Sky Garden reward dispatcher commits intent before forced child-process exit; fresh MapService recovery delivers once
Forced process exit after SQL commit/before queue acknowledgement replays the receipt without another letter
Real reward SQL rejection retains its queued intent; a new process completes delivery after fault removal

remaining: This protects each accepted letter from the SQL enqueue boundary. Occupation, selecting/enqueuing every recipient, player/guild points and World publication still do not share one durable war-result identity/transaction. A crash before a letter is enqueued can still lose it; re-running the whole event creates new letter IDs and is not deduplicated by these receipts.
Active-war phase/power/god-ball/point/participant reconstruction, World result receipts and cross-Map war ownership remain incomplete. See Gameforge/territory-wars.json.

World notifications now use the Wolverine transactional outbox and World actor inbox (Gameforge/wolverine-mail.json). The native client popup remains best effort across disconnects; durable mailbox contents remain available on reload.
Existing-item refund transfers and ordinary player mail are not converted here; the full cash exchange/contract lifecycle is not made atomic by protecting newly created replacement letters.

Source and migrations are deployed; startup and SQL schema checks pass. Full player-state worker shutdown/restart, multi-client war playthrough and compatible publisher/client data acceptance remain required.
implementation_history_note: The implementation and validation list below records the version-3 queue layer. Current production MailOperator uses Wolverine SQL transport; legacy rows forward the same operation IDs only after durable acceptance. Native transaction/receipt guarantees are reused, and the World notification outbox now shares the native SQL commit.
